items.title: Bobby Johnson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998
items.q: some of the songs like the Tommy Dorsey Band, Artie Shaw, Duke Ellington and even Benny Carter, we did on disk

ctx.x: Yeah. Pass the mege. That was the megaphone. And then all of a sudden, one night, they put up this megaphone and then we played. And in my career, I could say starting with early one morning at Decca Records in 1953 when all this stuff, I saw it all happen. I saw the first wire recorder, I saw the first time on tape, the first time anything — well naturally, I’m 83 years old. And every time we went, now you’ve got to remember that we were with RCA Victor for many years. Erskine’s band was with RCA Victor for ten.…
Well the bands knew how to balance themselves, didn’t they? You know, from playing live all that time.
